Hitherto there has been no confirmation of the persistent statements from Chinese and Japanese news agencies that Marshal Wu Pei-fu has been wounded or of the North China Daily News "official" wire from Peking stating that Wu Pei-fu is virtually a prisoner.
One report states that he was struck in the chest by a spent bullet but anyway he is still apparently directing the "defence of Hankow.

label: text
text: It now appears that the Southernerse penetrated" Wuchang on Wednesday and that fighting continued in and around Wuchang and the Wuchang Lakes.

label: text
text: The Southerners are hampered by the heavy rains and very boggy ground but Reuter's Peking correspondent wires that according to foreign official sources Wuchang tell on Friday. Wu Pei-fu, after retreating to Hankow, declared martial law and installed a new Civil Governor. The garrison commander at Hankow o: "Wu Pei-fu's forces is mounting artillery on Tortoise Hill. Hanyang, which commands the Wuchang side of the river and is making every preparation for a determined defence of Hanyang and Hankow. Reinforcements continue to arrive from the North. Reuter.

label: text
text: A report from Swallow says that Fukien forces are marching on Swatow, from which the "Reds" are fleeing.

label: text
text: A steamer is at present in the harbour waiting to carry the "Red" leaders southward.

label: text
text: The Wu Pei-fuite, Yang-sen, has commanded two British steamers at Wan-Hsien for the purpose of transporting troops to Chungking.

label: text
text: A report from Hankow says that he attack on Wuchang continued throughout Friday morning without appreciable result.

label: text
text: As an example of the heaviness of the bombardment the last telegram mentioned that the American Church and the General Hospital at Wuchang were hit twenty times.

label: text
text:
A Chinese military report says that the fighting in Wuchang was most severe yesterday afternoon, shells constantly falling on the city.
The telegraph staff were removed to Hankow from where only gun fine was audible at nine o'clock, but the Northerners still held the city.

label: text
text: Another report says that the Southerners drew to the front all the Changsha garrison, whilst Sun Chuan-fang (Wu Peifu's ally) has gathered 50,000 troops on the border ready to occupy Changsha.

label: text
text: The excitement in Hankow was growing yesterday evening but there was no disorder.—Reuter.

label: text
text: A British official wireless message from Hankow states that Wuchang was still in the hands of the Northerners this (Saturday) morning.—Reuter.

label: text
text: According to a telegram received by a Japanese shipping firm from Hankow this morning, a Japanese vessel witnessed at 3.30 o'clock on Thursday afternoon the British river gunboat Scarab in action with the Southern troops near Huachingkung, 50 miles up from Hankow, exchanging fire for more than two hours.—Reuter.

label: text
text: The situation in China and particularly at Hankow, in which neighbourhood a struggle is proceeding between Northern Chihli, troops and Cantonese forces, is being closely watched in London.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: The newspapers report the foreign Concessions in Hankow have been placed in a state of defence as a precaution and that the Japanese have landed a force from gunboats to protect their Conces.

label: text
text: sion. British naval vessels are stationed at Hankov and on the upper reaches of the Yangtse for the protection of British interests.

label: text
text: "The "Huang Po", publishes a telegram from Hankow reporting

label: text
text: that Hupen troops from Ichang and Chingchow are co-operating with Sun Chuan-fan's forces from Kiangsi. They occupied Changsha on the 4th inst., finding no enemy troops there. The telegram adds that the Southerners have also evacuated Yochow.

label: text
text: According to another Chinese telegram, the Southerners are retreating from Wuchang. The absence of official confirmation of this news should cause it to be received guardedly.

label: text
text: It is reported that Kuo Ying-chieh died yesterday, and that Wu Pei-fu appointed Tien Wei-chin Tupan of Honan. The report adds that Kuo was worn out by heavy work and succumbed to a complaint from which he had been sufferin; for a considerable time.—Reut...

label: text
text:
The P. and O. s.s.o. "Nagpore" arrived here to-day and reported that on Thursday, when twenty miles below Hankow, she was severely fired on by Cantonese troops. Nobody was injured, but the wooden deck was splintered.
It transpires that the seizure of two of Messrs. Butterfield and Swire's steamers at Wanhsen, mentioned last night, was merely an act of local officialdom. the allegation being that they were responsible for sinking a junk. It is believed to be an attempt at "squeeze."—Reuter.

label: text
text: A telegram received in Shanghai states that Jardine, Matheson's steamer "Kaiwo" has been taken over by the British Navy and fitted for active service". This, it is believed, is in connection with the seizure of two of Butterfield and Swire's steamers mentioned

label: text
text: ence of the Trade Union Congress at Bournemouth Mr. Arthur Pugh, President, dwelt largely on the General Strike. He declared that the weapon would not be left unused when it was sought to enforce upon any section of the workers terms which had not been made the subject of negotiation and collective agreement.

label: text
text:
The Congress had not met in a penitential mood nor with any consciousness of defeat. He claimed that the by-elections, especially of Hammersmith and Wallsend, had shown that Labour commanded increasing support and that it was not the Trade Unions but the Government that had lost the confidence of the people.
Referring to Labour's International policy, Mr. Pugh said that great and new problems were emerging in the change of direction of the main stream of emigration from Europe to undeveloped countries overseas, adding:—“We must bear in mind that our international organisation is mainly European in its structure and range. It is imperative that we should extend it to workers in these new countries whither the outflow of population from the older lands must inevitably tend in the future.” Practical consideration should be given to the question of obtaining International Trade Union agreements and understandings by which, combined with prevention of the importation of products of sweated labour, Trade Unionism in countries, where low economic standards prevailed, would be assisted by stronger countries and build up an effective organisation for the benefit of ill-paid and exploited workers.

Halifax (Nova Scotia), Sept. 5.
The "Nova Scotia," of the McMillan Arctic Expedition, on behalf of the Field Museum, has been safely anchored at Sydney, Cape Breton Harbour.

label: text
text: Commander. McMillan reported successful trip. The farthest north point reached was Diskaland, off the coast of Greenland, and many scientific specimens of are fish and bird life have been secured.—Regter's American Service.

Bogotas, Colombia, September 6
Over five thousand employees of
the Government Pacific Coast Railway
are striking. All traffic has
leased and many factories have
been shut. The stevedores at Porta
Buenventura have joined the
strikers.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Communal riot occurred in the Watgunge suburb, several persons being injured including one European and one Indian Police officer. Over 100 arrests have been made.

label: text
text: A Hindu procession with a band was nearing a Mosque when the Mohammedans summoned the Hindus to stop the music. The Hindus refused, whereupon fighting ensued, the Hindus marching past playing music.

label: text
text: Both Sides were reinforced and the police charged the rioters.—Reuter.

label: text
text: As the result of a typhoon passenger train from Tokyo to Nagoya was overturned near Tamamatsu this morning. There were only a few minor casualties. The roof of a school at Hamamatsu was blown off.

label: text
text: The typhoon is expected to strike Tokyo this afternoon.

label: text
text: Incoming reports show that the damage was widespread. Communications were upset. At the military aerodrome at Akenogahara, near Nagoya, forty aeroplanes were wrecked, several completely.

label: text
text: At Toyohashi a school collapsed, pinning down children and killing twelve, seriously injuring twenty. Three hundred houses were inundated.

label: text
text: In the Tochigi prefecture of Yoshida, forty buildings were destroyed, including the police station. Three policemen and several others were seriously injured.

label: text
text: At Kawasaki, near Yokohama, two lighters capzized and fifteen persons were drowned.

label: text
text: Forty houses were blown down at Saitama, and five were killed this morning.

label: text
text: Yokohama sailings, including the Siberia Maru, have been held up, owing to the severity of the gale. — Reuter.

label: text
text: Telegrams from Indo-China report that on the 2nd inst., the Cantonese Strike Committee at Tonghing, Kwangtung, seized the whole of the petroleum stocks of the French Compagnie Franco-Asiatique des Petroles of Haiphong, and announced their intention of selling the stocks at auction. The local authorities, having disregarded the French Consul's protests, the French Legation has now addressed a strong Note to the Waichiaopu asking that orders be given for the immediate restitution of the goods, and holding the Chinese authorities responsible for the consequences of this unlawful act and for reparation for all the losses sustained by the Company.—Reuter.

label: text
text: The Sunday Times states that there is a strong movement on foot in commercial circles interested in British-Indian trade to establish India House in London on similar lines to Australia House and Canada House.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: Three Courts-martial are being held at the Naval Barracks at Devonport in the course of the week arising out of the loss of Submarine H.29.—Reuter.
